title: Hubble's $1.5 billion blurry mirror
caption:
NASA launched a $1.5 billion space telescope and the first pictures came back blurry. 🔭
The mirror's edge was ground 2.2 microns too flat because the instrument used to test it was assembled 1.3 mm out: light from the edge and the centre focused in different places (spherical aberration).
Was fixing it in space genius, or should it never have launched?
first_comment: Humanity's greatest telescope needed glasses before it could see anything. Relatable 👓
sources: NASA Science, 'Hubble Servicing Mission 1': the primary mirror's outer edge was too flat by about 2.2 microns (spherical aberration); corrected by COSTAR and WFPC2 installed in December 1993

NASA, 'The Hubble Space Telescope Optical Systems Failure Report' (Allen Report, 1990): the reflective null corrector used to test the mirror was assembled with a 1.3 mm spacing error, so the mirror was precisely made to the wrong shape
Hubble cost about $1.5 billion at launch in April 1990 (NASA)
